name: MoE-Lightning: High-Throughput MoE Inference on Memory-constrained GPUs
problem: MoE's low per-token FLOPs make it attractive on paper, but its size puts it out of reach on anything below a high-end GPU, so in practice the whole point of the architecture is unavailable to the people who would benefit most from it.
mechanism: A CPU-GPU-I/O PIPELINING schedule called CGOPipe, paired with PAGED WEIGHTS, so that weights, CPU compute, GPU compute and I/O are all kept busy simultaneously instead of being serialized into phases. The second contribution is more useful to a reader than the system: a HIERARCHICAL ROOFLINE MODEL (HRM) that predicts achievable throughput from a memory hierarchy instead of requiring measurement, and a policy search driven by it. HRM is the transferable idea - it is the mechanism-level equivalent of the repo's existing FLOP-class records, applied to a three-level memory system, and it is why the paper can claim policies beating prior systems without a per-hardware tuning campaign. Paged weights are the enabler: they make expert weights pageable, which is what lets I/O overlap compute at all.
speedup_reported: Paper's own claim: up to 10.3x higher throughput than state-of-the-art offloading-enabled LLM inference systems for Mixtral 8x7B on a SINGLE T4 GPU (16 GB); when theoretical throughput is GPU-memory-bound it reaches the throughput upper bound with 2-3x less CPU memory; and it supports Mixtral 8x22B and DBRX on 2-4 T4s. The 10.3x is against OFFLOADING-ENABLED baselines, which are a weak and fast-moving class - against a modern tensor-parallel deployment on one T4 the gap is smaller, and the paper's scope is not that comparison.
notes:
RECORDED AS arxiv-preprint WITH venue_track 'unknown' - VENUE SEARCH EXPLICITLY NEGATIVE, AND THIS IS THE MOST LIKELY RECORD IN THE BATCH TO HAVE BEEN GIVEN AN INVENTED VENUE. MoE-Lightning is widely cited and has an ML-systems venue history, so it is precisely the paper where 'oh that was an OSDI/MLSys paper' would be the easy wrong answer. WHAT WAS CHECKED: OpenReview holds ONE record for this title and it is the arXiv deposit itself - venue 'CoRR 2024', venueid 'dblp.org/journals/CORR/2024' - which is not a venue claim about publication. Corpus checks, all negative: PMLR v267 (ICML 2025) contains no MoE-Lightning entry; MLSys 2025 (61 papers) and MLSys 2026 (135 papers) contain none; NeurIPS 2024 (4493 papers) contains none. arXiv 2411.11217's comment field is EMPTY. So arxiv-preprint/unknown with confidence 0.75 is the honest record. WHY IT IS STILL A GAP WORTH FILLING: the repo has no MoE weight-offload paper with a performance MODEL in it, and HRM is the artifact a capacity planner could actually reuse. HARDWARE FIELD DELIBERATELY DOES NOT NAME THE PAPER'S OWN GPU: the testbed is a single NVIDIA T4 (16 GB), and this repo has NO T4 accelerator record, so rather than invent an id or substitute an H100 - which would silently misrepresent the paper's own platform - the field lists only accelerators that exist in data/accelerators/ (nvidia-a10, nvidia-a100-80gb-sxm4) and this note states the real one. Anyone adding a T4 record should repoint this field at it.

confidence 0.75 -> 0.88. WAVE 4 SAID OF THIS RECORD: 'RECORDED AS arxiv-preprint ... DESPITE BEING WIDELY CITED

WHY WAVE 4'S SEARCH WAS EXECUTED CORRECTLY AND STILL MISSED IT - the generalisable lesson, and the reason this
is worth more than a venue field. Wave 4 checked OpenReview, PMLR v267 (ICML 2025), MLSys 2025 and 2026, and
NeurIPS 2024. Every one of those checks was right and every one of them has a blind spot: ASPLOS proceedings
are deposited with ACM under a DOI and appear in NONE of the OpenReview index, PMLR, or the four conference
indexes swept. A negative result across four corpora is only as strong as the union of what those corpora
index. For a paper outside ML/NeurIPS-style venues, the ACM DL via Crossref is the channel, and nobody was
looking there. This is the same shape as the PMLR-volume trap already logged in this repo, inverted: there the
index gave a confidently wrong venue; here the index gave a confidently EMPTY answer.

IDENTIFICATION IS EXACT, AND THE RAW TITLE WOULD HAVE FAILED A STRING CHECK: ACM renders 'MoE-Lightning' with
the L of Lightning as an \textsc small-caps span, so the deposit's title string is literally 'MoE-L\n
<scp>ightning</scp>\n : High-Throughput MoE Inference on' - multi-line, tagged, and not equal to the arXiv
title under any normalised comparison. Identity rests on (a) the distinctive subtitle 'High-Throughput MoE
Inference on Memory-constrained GPUs', (b) all NINE author names in arXiv order - Shiyi Cao, Shu Liu, Tyler
Griggs, Peter Schafhalter, Xiaoxuan Liu, Ying Sheng, Joseph E. Gonzalez, Matei Zaharia, Ion Stoica - matching the
arXiv API response for 2411.11217, and (c) a plausible ASPLOS page range. Author overlap ALONE would have been
insufficient here: the nine-name list also contains Ion Stoica and Joseph E. Gonzalez, who appear on many
Berkeley systems papers.
